name: Satyendra Nath Bose
teaser: The Indian physicist who derived Planck's radiation law with a new way of counting particles — work Einstein seized upon, spawning 'Bose–Einstein statistics' and the particles we now call bosons. His letter to Einstein changed physics.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Bose counted photons differently, letting them share the same quantum state. Write what a Bose–Einstein condensate is and why particles that obey his statistics are named bosons.

name: C. V. Raman
teaser: The Indian physicist who discovered that light changes color slightly when it scatters off molecules — the Raman effect, now the basis of a whole analytical technique. He won the 1930 Nobel, the first Asian scientist to do so.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Raman, working with simple equipment and sunlight, found inelastic scattering of light by molecules. Write how Raman spectroscopy fingerprints molecules today, from drugs to art.

name: Meghnad Saha
teaser: The Indian astrophysicist whose Saha equation explains the ionization states of atoms in stars — how temperature reveals a star's composition. His 1920 formula let astronomers read the periodic table in starlight.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the Saha equation connects temperature to the ionization of atoms in stellar atmospheres. Write how it let Cecilia Payne and others decode what stars are made of.

name: Emilio Segrè
teaser: The Italian-American physicist who discovered the antiproton and co-discovered technetium and astatine. He worked on the Manhattan Project and co-wrote the Fermi diary that documented the first nuclear chain reaction.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Segrè and Chamberlain found the antiproton at Berkeley's Bevatron in 1955. Write why antimatter must exist as a mirror image of matter and how it annihilates on contact.

name: Luis Alvarez
teaser: The American physicist who used radar to land planes blind, invented the spark chamber, and then shocked the world by proposing an asteroid killed the dinosaurs — sealed with an iridium layer found with his geologist son.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the Alvarez team found iridium in the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary layer. Write how the Chicxulub crater confirmed the impact and what the extinction event tells us about planetary danger.

name: Ernest Lawrence
teaser: The American physicist who invented the cyclotron, a particle accelerator that spirals protons to high energies — making nuclear physics a laboratory science. His Radiation Lab at Berkeley produced a dozen Nobel laureates.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the cyclotron accelerates particles in expanding spiral orbits using magnetic and electric fields. Write how it enabled the discovery of new elements and why it earned Lawrence the 1939 Nobel.

name: Leo Szilard
teaser: The Hungarian physicist who conceived the nuclear chain reaction while waiting at a London traffic light, then pushed Einstein to warn Roosevelt about it — and spent the rest of his life opposing the weapon it made. He also invented the refrigerator that keeps food cold.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Szilard realized that neutron emission from fission could sustain a chain reaction. Write how the Einstein–Szilard letter led to the Manhattan Project and how Szilard campaigned to stop the bomb's use.

name: Eugene Wigner
teaser: The Hungarian-American physicist who applied symmetry to quantum mechanics, earning the 1963 Nobel. He also designed the graphite reactor that produced the first self-sustaining chain reaction — and marveled at the 'unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics.'

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Wigner used group theory to classify particles and symmetries in quantum mechanics. Write what his phrase about mathematics' unreasonable effectiveness means and how symmetry guides modern physics.

name: John Wheeler
teaser: The American physicist who coined the terms 'black hole' and 'wormhole,' worked with Bohr on fission, and tutored Feynman. His student-centric teaching shaped a generation — and his thought experiments pushed physics to its edges.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Wheeler coined 'black hole' in 1967 and explored the idea's consequences with his students. Write what a black hole is and why 'it from bit' was his famous slogan about information.

name: David Bohm
teaser: The American physicist whose 'Bohmian mechanics' offered a hidden-variables picture of quantum reality and whose plasma research revealed collective behavior. His 1952 interpretation remains the main rival to the Copenhagen view.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Bohm's interpretation keeps particles with definite positions, guided by a quantum wave. Write how it differs from standard quantum mechanics and why it was long dismissed.

name: Alice Ball
teaser: The African American chemist who, at 23, developed the 'Ball Method' — the first effective injectable treatment for leprosy, extracted from chaulmoogra oil. She died young, and her achievement was credited to a man for decades.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Alice Ball made chaulmoogra oil's active esters water-soluble for injection. Write why the disease was feared, how her method transformed treatment, and how her credit was restored.

name: Esther Lederberg
teaser: The American microbiologist who discovered lambda phage, a virus that lives silently inside bacteria — the key to gene regulation and one of biology's favorite tools. Her replica-plating method made her husband's Nobel-winning work possible.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Esther Lederberg invented replica plating with velvet, transferring colonies between plates. Write what lambda phage is and how it became a model for understanding gene switching.

name: Gladys West
teaser: The American mathematician who did the painstaking calculations on the Navy's satellites that made GPS possible, then wrote the data-processing that refined the Earth's precise shape. Her work helps you find your way every day.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Gladys West processed satellite data to model the Earth's geoid precisely. Write how GPS uses satellites and time to fix your position and why her calculations were essential.

name: Yvonne Brill
teaser: The Canadian-American rocket scientist who invented the electrothermal hydrazine thruster, keeping communication satellites in orbit with a trickle of fuel. Her design became standard on satellites worldwide.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Brill's thruster used electrical heat to double the efficiency of hydrazine fuel for satellite station-keeping. Write why this invention extended satellite lifetimes and how she broke into aerospace.

name: Williamina Fleming
teaser: The Scottish maid-turned-astronomer who sorted the spectra of over 10,000 stars at Harvard and discovered the Horsehead Nebula. She created the first classification system for stellar spectra and trained a generation of women 'computers.'

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Fleming developed a letter scheme for stellar spectra while cataloging the sky at Harvard. Write what the Horsehead Nebula is and how the Harvard Computers advanced astronomy.

name: Ruby Payne-Scott
teaser: The Australian radio astronomer who made the first radio observations of the Sun and discovered solar bursts, laying the groundwork for radio astronomy — and fought her own employer for equal pay and maternity rights.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Payne-Scott used a cliff-top antenna to detect radio bursts from the Sun. Write what solar radio emission tells us about the Sun's activity and why she is a pioneer of radio astronomy.

name: Katharine Burr Blodgett
teaser: The American physicist who invented non-reflective glass — layering films so thin they cancel glare — now used in eyeglasses, camera lenses, and screens. She was the first woman to earn a PhD in physics from Cambridge.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Blodgett built up molecular layers of soap film to make glass transmit light without reflection. Write how her 'invisible glass' improved optics and why her Langmuir–Blodgett films matter in labs today.

name: Edith Clarke
teaser: The American electrical engineer who made power systems safe to compute, inventing the Clarke calculator — a graphical tool for solving transmission-line equations. She was the first woman electrical engineer hired by GE and first female IEEE Fellow.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Edith Clarke's calculator and her 1943 textbook simplified power transmission analysis. Write why her work on long-distance power lines mattered as grids grew across America.

name: Hedy Lamarr
teaser: The Hollywood star who, with composer George Antheil, patented frequency hopping — rapidly switching radio channels so torpedoes couldn't be jammed. Her idea became the foundation of Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Lamarr and Antheil's 1942 patent used 88 piano-like channels to hop radio frequencies. Write how spread spectrum makes Wi-Fi and Bluetooth robust and why her contribution was recognized late.

name: François Jacob
teaser: The French biologist who, with Jacques Monod, discovered how genes get switched on and off — the operon model — earning the 1965 Nobel. A war hero who lost his leg fighting the Nazis, he later wrote moving memoirs.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the lac operon controls lactose metabolism in E. coli, with repressors and inducers. Write how gene regulation works and why this model transformed molecular biology.

name: Jacques Monod
teaser: The French biochemist who co-discovered messenger RNA's role and the lac operon, showing cells read their genes on demand. His philosophical essay Chance and Necessity argued life is the product of chance and natural law.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Monod and Jacob discovered that a messenger molecule carries genetic instructions from DNA to the ribosome. Write how messenger RNA works and why it connects DNA to proteins.
